what_its_for: Acarbose is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by slowing down the digestion of carbohydrates (starches and sugars) in your food, which helps prevent your blood sugar from rising too quickly after meals. It is usually used along with diet, exercise, and sometimes other diabetes medicines.
how_to_take: Take acarbose by mouth with the first bite of each main meal, three times a day. Swallow the tablet whole or chew it slightly with your first bite of food. Do not take it before or after a meal — it must be taken at the start of eating to work properly. Always follow the meal and diet plan your doctor or dietitian has given you.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose (25 mg three times a day with meals) and slowly increase it over several weeks to find the right dose for you. The usual maintenance dose is 50 mg to 100 mg three times a day with meals. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose but have not started eating your meal yet, take it as soon as you remember at the beginning of that meal. If you have already finished your meal, skip the missed dose completely — do not double up or take it between meals. Wait until your next meal to take your next regular dose.
storage: Store acarbose at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of sugary or starchy foods, as this can make your blood sugar harder to control. Do not drink alcohol excessively, as it can affect your blood sugar levels. If you experience low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) while taking acarbose — especially if you are also taking other diabetes medicines like insulin or sulfonylureas — treat it with pure glucose (glucose tablets or gel), NOT table sugar, candy, or fruit juice, because acarbose slows the breakdown of regular sugar. Avoid taking antacids or digestive enzyme products (like amylase or pancreatin) at the same time as acarbose, as they can reduce how well it works.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); signs of very low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, confusion, or rapid heartbeat that do not improve with glucose treatment; unusual tiredness or dark-colored urine; severe or ongoing diarrhea or gas that does not improve. Also tell your doctor about any new medicines you start taking.
when_it_works: Acarbose starts working with your very first dose by slowing sugar absorption after meals. However, you may not notice a big change in how you feel right away. Blood sugar improvements can be seen within the first few weeks, but it may take 2 to 3 months of regular use, combined with healthy eating and exercise, to see the full benefit. Your doctor will check your blood sugar and HbA1c levels regularly to track how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Acarbose can generally be used safely in older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney problems: Acarbose is NOT recommended if you have significant kidney disease (creatinine levels above 2 mg/dL). Talk to your doctor. Liver problems: Acarbose is NOT recommended if you have liver disease or cirrhosis. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Acarbose is generally not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor about safer options for managing your blood sugar during these times. Children: Acarbose is not approved for use in children.
